what: the first wave of ports made from the guide alone, for ocaml and lua (port, independent review, fix, verify), and the consolidated account of all four ports

digest.part: Wave 1 of the ports made from the guide alone (interface version 3.2, base32 tag v32-frozen): the ocaml and lua pipelines in full (port, independent review, fix, independent verify), plus the consolidated account of all four wave-1 ports (perl, swift, ocaml, lua) in s3b-wave1-consolidated.md. All records named in the instructions were present and read completely. Context read: brief.md (H1-H5), brief6.md (the round these ports ran in), the opening of brief7.md (which summarises this wave), and the opening of prompts j-port/j-review/j-fix.

rounds.purpose: Port ocaml's README tutorial, root quick start and REFERENCE to the shared code using only the porting guide v3.2: a naming hook, a syntax provider, the porter's part of the forms file, and deletion of the three old components. Then review the output with the one command (portcheck) until it passes.
rounds.produced: sdkgen commits 146c2abc, a21aeb2a, 1e9cf150; tools fa9c146. Syntax_ocaml.ts (237 lines) and Naming_ocaml.ts (24) replace 723 deleted lines. Normal-mode portcheck PASS; SCRATCH mode exit 1. 5 interface gaps recorded, none made. 4 runtime-table or guide rows found wrong. 236 classes decided by hand. Reported ok: False, only because scratch mode cannot pass.
rounds.changed: No shared file touched. The porter changed okFalse from the guide's 'false' to 'Bool false'. Statements now print as top-level definitions, so the root quick start is a valid file. Operation signatures are unnamed `(value) (value)`, and a note carries the parameter names.

rounds.purpose: Independent adversarial read of the ocaml port: audit every fact against the runtime, compare OLD and NEW pages, re-run the porter's commands, and attack the process with mutations.
rounds.produced: Verdict: accept-with-fixes. Every porter number reproduced. Full suite run (2601 tests). A whole OCaml SDK generated from base and port: only README.md and REFERENCE.md differ. 24 source mutations, 3 page edits and 1 no-edit control. 10 required fixes: 3 in ocaml's own files, 7 needing a shared file. 6 process holes listed as not caught.
rounds.changed: Found the cancel absence check blind: its search left out Entity_ocaml.ts. Found the e_match_get copy unstated, one hand reason false, and a dropped clause recorded as restored. Found 4 false or awkward sentences on the page (`direct()`, 'Return the entity name.' for a field, 'Instance functions', the `(value) (value)` headings). Explained the porter's unexplained 21.4% tutorial share as a masking artifact.

rounds.purpose: Apply the reviewer's fixes that sit in ocaml's own files and record the rest as shared changes, without making them.
rounds.who: one fixer (not the porter or the reviewer)
rounds.produced: sdkgen 6c467124 and tools 812357d. 3 findings fixed (cancel absence, 1 hand reason, 2 hand records). 7 findings plus the guide recorded as needing shared changes (9 entries in shared_changes_needed). Page output byte-identical to the porter's. Reported ok: False, because scratch mode still exits 1.
rounds.changed: The cancel absence now covers Entity_ocaml.ts, with the 4 stream `signal` lines excused verbatim: 8 of 8 probe controls are found. Records 6624c1429f and 53f65fd5c6 changed from restored:shared to dropped. The f64ae2f4fc reason was corrected. The fixer declined the optional `let () = try ... with` change, which would have turned 19 byte-identical blocks into unverifiable changed ones.

rounds.purpose: Independent check that the ocaml port stands at its last commit: re-run everything and attack it again.
rounds.produced: Reported ok: True. Every number matched the fixer's. 2 fresh attacks (a1 test_with arity, a2 integer type word): both failed the one command, but neither failed the guard. 10 still-wrong items and 10 shared changes handed over.
rounds.changed: Confirmed all 3 fixes. Added two guard holes: test-call arity is unchecked, and the provider's type mapping is checked by nothing but the OLD-page ledger. Noted weak points in the new cancel pattern: the excuses are not tied to a file, and names such as `stop_signal`, `interrupt ()` and `timeout_abort` are not matched.

rounds.purpose: Port lua by the guide v3.2, the same way as ocaml.
rounds.produced: sdkgen d1fe7418, 664994ef, fa2ffcac; tools 59dfdba, bce2d23. Syntax_lua.ts (164 lines) and Naming_lua.ts (26) replace 749 deleted lines. Normal-mode portcheck PASS; SCRATCH exit 1. 2 interface gaps (accessor cache, purity PRINTING list). 5 runtime-table rows wrong. 174 classes decided by hand. Reported ok: True.
rounds.changed: No shared source file touched. Only lua's own lines of the shared test lua-table-keys.test.ts and of the golden changed. The porter corrected the forms reader so the operations' second return value is named `err`, not 'second value'. The porter decided prints 'fields' by hand, so the root quick start drops OLD's json.encode.

rounds.purpose: Independent adversarial read of the lua port.
rounds.produced: Verdict: accept-with-fixes. Every porter number reproduced. 20 attacks (15 source mutations, 5 page mutations): 19 failed the one command, 1 passed. 9 required fixes: 4 in lua's files, 5 shared. 4 process holes listed as not caught.
rounds.changed: Found 1 hand record that hid a contradiction (d2b1853b85), 2 citations that do not show their value (ctor[0], pairForm), and a cancel absence search scoped to fetcher.lua only. Found 2 shared sentences false for lua: the accessor sentence and direct's `err` clause. Corrected the porter's doubt: ProjectNameError does have __tostring.

rounds.purpose: Apply the lua-side fixes and record the shared ones.
rounds.produced: sdkgen 8478f2dc (forms only, +17/-5); tools f0c2d47 and 72881b6. 4 fixed in lua files, 5 recorded as shared, 1 new shared change found (the stream-signal sentence). In all, 7 shared changes recorded. No generated page changed. Reported ok: True.
rounds.changed: d2b1853b85 is now a contradiction, so reference contradictions went from 1 to 2 and by-hand from 52 to 51. The ctor[0] and pairForm citations now quote code. The cancel fact was narrowed to operations: the search now covers Main.fragment.lua, the 6 op fragments, tm/lua/utility/ and tm/lua/core/, and leaves out Entity.fragment.lua.

rounds.purpose: Independent check of the lua port at its last commit.
rounds.produced: Reported ok: True. All numbers matched; guard and reader 65/65 across all languages. 2 fresh attacks: A1 not caught at all, A2 caught. 5 still-wrong items and 7 shared changes handed over.
rounds.changed: Showed that the fixer's claim that the cancel search covers 'every file an operation runs through' is false. Entity.fragment.lua holds `_run_op` and `_run_steps`, and an operation-cancel check added there passed the guard 65/65.

rounds.purpose: Gather, per language, everything the sixteen wave-1 reports (four stages for each of perl, swift, ocaml and lua) say must change outside a port, as input to the merge round (brief 7).
rounds.who: generated by a script from the sixteen structured results; it decides nothing
rounds.produced: s3b-wave1-consolidated.md. Stage outcomes: perl port ok=True, review accept-with-fixes, fix ok=False, verify ok=False. swift port ok=True, review accept-with-fixes, fix ok=True, verify ok=False. ocaml port ok=False, review accept-with-fixes, fix ok=False, verify ok=True. lua port ok=True, review accept-with-fixes, fix ok=True, verify ok=True.

findings.finding: All four wave-1 ports were written from the guide alone, and none edited shared code. Each passed the one command with its own hand records, and the reviewers, fixers and verifiers reproduced every reported number. No other language's output changed.
findings.source: s3b-review-ocaml.txt summary; s3b-review-lua.txt summary; s3b-verify-ocaml.txt other_languages; s3b-verify-lua.txt other_languages

findings.finding: Source shrank in every case. ocaml went from 723 to 261 lines (2.77x; 2.2x counting forms and generator edits), lua from 749 to 190 (3.9x), perl from 735 to 213 (3.45x) and swift from 764 to 195 (3.9x). Counting forms, every language except ocaml is at or above 3.1x, and all are above H2's 2x threshold.
findings.source: s3b-port-ocaml.txt lines; s3b-port-lua.txt lines; s3b-wave1-consolidated.md perl and swift 'Lines, prose (porter)'

findings.finding: Per-language prose stayed far under H1's 15% line. Provider literals and notes are 7.3% of ocaml's words, 4.3% of lua's, 1.8% literals plus 1.6% notes for perl, and 0.6% for swift. All three ocaml notes exist only to make up for interface gaps.
findings.source: s3b-review-ocaml.txt interface; s3b-port-lua.txt prose; s3b-wave1-consolidated.md perl and swift prose

findings.finding: Passing every check did not mean the pages were right. The independent reviewers found false shared sentences for runtimes nobody had ported before: ocaml's `direct()`, 'Return the entity name.' for a field and 'Instance functions' over module functions; lua's 'Create a new instance' where nil returns a cached one, and '`err` holds the error' where a non-2xx response leaves err unset. Each needs a new optional fact or slot in shared code. Until those land, the sentences stay false on every page of that language.

None of the shared changes the ports need was made during the wave. The fixers recorded them for one integrator: ocaml 9 entries, lua 7, perl 3, swift 6. All are additive except two swift ones, which count as breaking only because they reword a shared sentence. The interface held without breaking changes, but its first contact with four new runtimes produced about two dozen additive changes.
findings.source: s3b-fix-ocaml.txt shared_changes_needed; s3b-fix-lua.txt shared_changes_needed; s3b-wave1-consolidated.md perl and swift 'Fixer: shared changes needed'

findings.finding: H4 is essentially untested for ocaml, lua and swift. 229, 226 and 172 changed block instances respectively were compiled by nothing, because no toolchain was present; reviewers read 23 and 24 distinct ocaml and lua blocks by eye and found none failing. perl, the one wave-1 language with a toolchain, has a NEW root quick start that fails `perl -c` from the repository root (Can't locate DemoSDK.pm), while its lane stays at 7/7.
findings.source: s3b-verify-ocaml.txt unverified; s3b-verify-lua.txt unverified; s3b-wave1-consolidated.md perl and swift verifier sections

findings.finding: The perl compile failure comes from the interface: the shared imports printer is not told whether it prints for the tutorial or the root quick start. The proposed fix is additive (an optional `place` on Scope plus a target-directory layout role) and has not been built or tested. A shared display-field helper also makes perl print HASH(0x...) in 17 variations.
findings.source: s3b-wave1-consolidated.md perl 'Fixer: shared changes needed', 'Verifier: still wrong'

findings.finding: The guard, the check meant to tie every declared fact to the runtime, has repeatable holes. A pinned value is compared only when it is prose, so ocaml 'false' passes against 'Bool false' and lua 'nil' against 'false'. It does not check the constructor or receiver form (lua `sdk.create`, `client.Planet()`), call arity (ocaml `test_with Noval`, swift `load(nil)`), or the provider's type words (ocaml int to float). Most such mutations were caught only by comparison with the OLD page or by block classes a person can accept by hand, so a port of a language with no OLD page would lose that net.
findings.source: s3b-review-ocaml.txt not_caught; s3b-review-lua.txt not_caught; s3b-verify-ocaml.txt attacks; s3b-wave1-consolidated.md swift 'Verifier: fresh attacks'

findings.finding: Some attacks passed the whole process. A shared sentence dropped from all 19 lua REFERENCEs gave PORTCHECK PASS. An operation-cancel check added to lua's _run_op passed the guard 65/65. In swift, a provider that failed to compile, or a generation that threw, was measured on stale output and reported PASS.
findings.source: s3b-review-lua.txt attacks[16]; s3b-verify-lua.txt attacks[0]; s3b-wave1-consolidated.md swift 'Reviewer: attacks nothing caught'

findings.finding: Hand judgement carries a large part of the check. Hundreds of classes per language are decided by a person (ocaml 236, lua 174), and 0 by rule. Scratch mode, which ignores hand records, cannot pass any port (ocaml OPEN 28/3/104, lua 23/3/71). Every one of the 79 shared sentences matched per language was a sentence nobody had reviewed. Independent reviewers found wrong hand records in both ocaml and lua.
findings.source: s3b-port-ocaml.txt hand_decisions, portcheck; s3b-port-lua.txt hand_decisions; s3b-review-ocaml.txt hand_records; s3b-review-lua.txt hand_records

findings.finding: The guide itself was wrong in places, and the porters had to correct it. It gave ocaml's okFalse as 'false' where the runtime writes `Bool false`, and lua's failure marker as 'second value', which no signature can spell. It promised that the one command passes in scratch mode, which no port can do. Its runtime table had 3 wrong ocaml rows and 5 wrong lua rows.
findings.source: s3b-port-ocaml.txt table_rows_wrong, guide_problems; s3b-port-lua.txt table_rows_wrong, guide_problems

findings.finding: The new pages fixed real defects of the old ones. They print a valid ocaml root quick start (OLD was invalid in ent-none and ref-issues), true test signatures, corrected step numbering, server variables and secrets, and every lua write checked. The catalogued corrections (S49, S50, S09, S13, S25, U45 and more) reached both languages through shared code with no per-language edit. They also lost things the interface cannot yet carry: ocaml's e_deleted marker and parameter names, lua's whole-record print, and swift's `list(nil, nil)`.
